outcome: Make the audio range refusals and tool instructions state what the reader actually accepts, and pin the requested-window policy in tests.
criteria: A track whose declared start is at or beyond its estimated endpoint is refused as an unknown extent, so no refusal recommends an inverted interval.
The entirely-before refusal marks an estimated endpoint and its source, as the past-end refusal already does.
The audio tool instructions distinguish an overlapping request, which is clamped to the track, from a wholly outside one, which is refused.
Regressions pin that the clip covers the requested window rather than the duration measured from the track start, and assert the FFmpeg cut matches that window.
Leading-silence assertions are tight enough to fail on a partial return of head padding.
Numeric request-identity fields are canonical floats, and the README states how each edge is established, including the head's reliance on declared track metadata.

dispositions.note: A declared track start at or after the container-derived endpoint now raises an unknown-extent refusal in _audio_bounds, so the inverted [15, 10) recommendation is unreachable.
The entirely-before refusal names the endpoint's source and marks it estimated, matching the past-end refusal.
The audio instructions now say an overlapping request is cut back to the track and only a wholly outside one is refused.
A new regression pins clip=(3, 4) for a [0, 4) request on a track starting at 3 and asserts the FFmpeg atrim window; reintroducing the drift fails it.
The PCM check requires the tone within a millisecond and the AAC check within 20 ms; reintroducing the head padding fails three tests.
video_origin_s and both audio_bounds endpoints are floats, and the README separates the measured endpoint from the declared start.

note: An independent review of PR 1 by an external model raised eight areas; these are the findings I could confirm. I reproduced the inverted-bounds refusal before changing anything: a track declaring a start past the container's estimated end told the caller to request an interval inside [15, 10) s, which teaches nothing, so the degenerate bounds are now refused where they are computed. The instructions given to the host model claimed any interval outside the bounds is refused, when an overlapping one is clamped; that wording is corrected. Two test gaps were real: nothing pinned duration_s to the requested window, so a drift to measuring it from the clamped start would have passed, and the leading-silence assertions were loose enough to admit a partial return of head padding. Both are now proved by reintroducing each defect and watching the suite fail. I declined the reviewer's suggestion to clamp the cut to the first decoded packet rather than the declared start_time: no real container exhibiting that mismatch could be produced, and the change would risk trimming genuine quiet, so the residual is documented instead. Interior gap padding is unchanged; it is pre-existing, required for segment alignment, and already disclosed. 272 tests pass with no skips.
